title: Embeddings client: Python/TS SDK improvements — pagination, robust error handling, typed responses
creator: Liam Chen
description: Improve the Embeddings SDK clients (Python and TypeScript) to provide: (1) server-side pagination helpers and deterministic client-side iterators for large embeddings/rerank requests; (2) consistent, typed response objects with documented shapes; (3) improved retry and error handling semantics with clear transient vs permanent classification; and (4) ergonomic defaults for batching and concurrency to reduce latency and cost. This ticket covers API design, reference implementation in both languages, tests, benchmarks, and migration notes for existing customers.
acceptance_criteria: Python and TS SDKs expose a single EmbeddingsIterator abstraction that transparently pages server responses and supports peek() and prefetch(n)
SDK response types include stable field names for vector, meta, and score, and are schema-documented in docstrings/typed defs
Transient network and rate-limit errors are retried with exponential backoff up to configurable limits; permanent errors surface descriptive exceptions with HTTP status and error code
Default client settings reduce tail latency by enabling small request-level batching and a concurrency cap; documented benchmarks show >=10% latency improvement for common workloads
Comprehensive unit and integration tests covering pagination, retries, error classification, and typing for both languages
Migration guide exists that maps old response shapes to new typed responses and lists breaking changes (if any)
test_plan: Unit tests for iterator behavior, edge cases (empty results, final page smaller than page_size), and error propagation. Integration test against sandbox embeddings endpoint with synthetic large corpus to validate pagination and prefetch. Backwards-compatibility tests against legacy response shapes. Load tests for default batching/concurrency knobs to collect p50/p95/p99 latency and token cost metrics.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge feature branches behind SDK feature flag; 2) Publish beta packages to npm and PyPI with beta tag; 3) Run dogfood tests with internal services (search, rerank pipelines); 4) Collect telemetry for errors and latency for 1 week; 5) Promote to stable release and announce migration notes in release notes and docs; 6) Monitor customer support channels for regressions and ship fastfixes if needed.
notes: Design decision: prefer an iterator-based client API instead of returning huge in-memory lists to support very large result sets and streaming rerank pipelines
Trade-off: typed responses increase surface area for breaking changes; we will provide a compatibility shim layer and opt-in strict typing in 2.0 release
Performance note: server-side page tokens will embed workload hints to allow the client to prefetch more aggressively when downstream consumers are batching requests
